2.0.77._note:
Captured on Factorio 2.0.77, which is the only thing this row needs: guest/go/data/engine.go keys on the RUNNING engine and not on the manifest, so a 2.1 binary produces the 2.1 flavour whatever the package says and any 2.0 binary produces this one from any tree. It was FIRST taken on the release/2.0 recut at 0.2.1; every re-capture since, this one included, was taken on TRUNK through the cross-series stamped path the header of test/check-datastage.py describes, because the branch never carried the customizer at all. So THIS ROW IS TRUNK'S 2.0-FLAVOUR EMISSION, not release/2.0's: the branch carries its own frozen copy of this file and nothing compares the two. Corrected 2026-09-09; the opening used to say the recut was the only place it could be taken, which the FIVE re-captures below had already contradicted (five arrows in the chain below, five RE-CAPTURED markers, and five trunk commits -- 50c0db3, 6ec3937, 33657f5, f3029b6, 3fd5875 -- after the first capture at ca9d448). What this line pins that the 2.1.16 one cannot is the three things the version branch turns ON -- `not_colliding_with_itself` on bbb-linked-belt's collision mask, the `bbb-can-stack` marker prototype, and a mod-settings dump carrying the runtime-global `bbb-multi-edge-parts` beside the two startup cost settings, where the 2.1 arm carries the two alone. Per engine and per mod set: the dump carries every prototype every mod defined. Only the DEFAULT settings are hashed; the variant and speed arms assert values. RE-CAPTURED FOR 0.3.3's RECIPE CUSTOMIZER, and only `mod_settings_sha256` moved (196275f867f7f8b5 -> 258d44de08b43c9e, the same on both mod sets): `bbb-recipe-cost` gained the value `custom` and a `localised_description` composed from its six presets, and `bbb-recipe-ingredients` joined it as a third setting at order `aa`. Both `data_raw_sha256` values are unmoved and the normalised data-raw dumps were compared byte for byte either side of the change, which is what says the customizer reaches the settings stage and nothing else while every setting is at its default. RE-CAPTURED AGAIN FOR 0.3.3's RESEARCH CUSTOMIZER, and again only `mod_settings_sha256` moved (258d44de08b43c9e -> 0bea93fa1594052e, the same on both mod sets): `bbb-tech-cost` gained the value `custom` and a `localised_description` composed from its three tiers, and three settings joined it at orders that sort after it -- `bbb-tech-packs`, a string-setting with `auto_trim` and its own composed description, at `ba`; `bbb-tech-count`, an int-setting with minimum_value 1 and maximum_value 1000000, at `bb`; and `bbb-tech-seconds`, a double-setting with minimum_value 1 and maximum_value 3600, at `bc`. Both `data_raw_sha256` values are unmoved and both arms' normalised data-raw dumps compare byte for byte either side of the change, which is what says the research customizer reaches the settings stage and nothing else while every setting is at its default. RE-CAPTURED FOR THE FkRecipes HEAD 9754f49, and only `mod_settings_sha256` moved (0bea93fa1594052e -> e5e7d159e88f4a6b, the same on both mod sets): `bbb-tech-cost`'s composed `localised_description` names each tier's technology through {"technology-name.<source>"} where it carried the internal name as plain text, and both `data_raw_sha256` values are unmoved with both arms' normalised data-raw dumps byte-identical either side of the change. RE-CAPTURED FOR THE SYNC PASS, WHICH MAKES THE CUSTOMIZER'S FOUR SETTINGS GENERATED NAMES PLACED BY `OrderAfter`, and again only `mod_settings_sha256` moved (e5e7d159e88f4a6b -> df4d6c3fc7bf854d, the same on both mod sets): `bbb-recipe-ingredients` is `better-belt-balancer-recipe-ingredients` at order `aab` where it was `aa`, `bbb-tech-packs` is `better-belt-balancer-tech-packs` at `bad` where it was `ba`, `bbb-tech-count` is `better-belt-balancer-tech-count` at `bae` where it was `bb` and `bbb-tech-seconds` is `better-belt-balancer-tech-seconds` at `baf` where it was `bc`, while the two dropdowns keep `bbb-recipe-cost` at `a` and `bbb-tech-cost` at `b`; both `data_raw_sha256` values are unmoved and both arms' normalised data-raw dumps were compared byte for byte either side of the change, which is what says the rename reaches the settings stage and nothing else. RE-CAPTURED FOR THE FkRecipes HEAD 0077f3c, WHOSE MOVE IS THE LIBRARY'S COMPOSED-DESCRIPTION SHAPE AND NOTHING OF THIS PLAN'S, and again only `mod_settings_sha256` moved (df4d6c3fc7bf854d -> aa75497e55ce4333, the same on both mod sets), in two places. `bbb-recipe-cost`'s composed `localised_description` separates each preset's label from its ingredient list with "
  type: " where it used ": ", so a preset spends two lines where it spent one and the whole description is 13 lines against 7, which is 1 + 6 x 2 against 1 + 6; and both text settings, `better-belt-balancer-recipe-ingredients` and `better-belt-balancer-tech-packs`, gain two sentences after their `
default: ...` line -- the 2000-character limit, and what becomes of a text this mod cannot use, which since FkRecipes 2e5f779 is set aside for this mod's own declaration rather than refusing the load. Both `data_raw_sha256` values are unmoved, and since that hash is taken over the whole normalised data-raw dump its being unmoved IS those dumps compared byte for byte, which is what says the library's change reaches the settings stage and nothing else. RE-CAPTURED FOR THE FkRecipes HEAD 221ff9c, WHOSE FIX ROUND 2 WITHDRAWS THE `custom` DROPDOWN VALUE AND MAKES THE TEXT BESIDE THE DROPDOWN THE SWITCH, and again only `mod_settings_sha256` moved (aa75497e55ce4333 -> b6e583e6163249ba, the same on both mod sets), in five places, every one of them read out of the engine's own settings dump rather than argued. ONE, `bbb-recipe-cost`'s `allowed_values` is six values where it was seven and `bbb-tech-cost`'s is three where it was four, both having lost `custom`. TWO, `better-belt-balancer-tech-seconds` is an `int-setting` where it was a `double-setting`, under the same name, and both research numbers declare `default_value` 0 and `minimum_value` 0 where they declared 20 with minimum 1 and 15 with minimum 1, because 0 is now what means the dropdown decides. THREE, both dropdowns' composed `localised_description` gains a closing line (`
The setting below applies instead while it does not say default.`) and the INGREDIENT one gains the wrap line before it, while both text settings gain the wrap line and a switch line of their own and the ingredient one's format line gains the `none` clause. FOUR, the two research numbers carry a composed `localised_description` where they carried none at all. FIVE, and it is the one that touches every composed description in the file, every locale key any of them references is now the engine's own fallback group `{"?", {"<section>.<key>"}, "<raw>"}` where it was the bare `{"<section>.<key>"}`, so the head line of all five composed descriptions, the nine preset labels and the three `technology-name` references each gained two elements; that is FkRecipes e4604d4, whose point is that a key the game does not define no longer costs the whole tooltip, and it supersedes the shape the 9754f49 paragraph above pins. Both `prototype_list_checksum` values are unmoved and both `data_raw_sha256` values are unmoved, and since the DATA-RAW hash is taken over the whole normalised dump its being unmoved IS those dumps compared byte for byte, which is what says the withdrawal reaches the settings stage and nothing else while every setting is at its default. RE-CAPTURED FOR THE FkRecipes HEAD cf66357, WHOSE FIX ROUND 3 GIVES THE LIBRARY THE LADDER DISCLOSURE THIS MOD'S OWN .cfg USED TO BE THE ONLY COPY OF, and again only `mod_settings_sha256` moved (b6e583e6163249ba -> f83e037d8f787dcf, the same on both mod sets), in three settings and nowhere else. THE RESULTING STATE IS READ OUT OF THE ENGINE'S OWN SETTINGS DUMP AND THE THREE DELTAS ARE NOT, because no pre-round dump is kept: each delta is read off the guest/go/tune/plan_test.go diff and then CHECKED BY RECONSTRUCTION, which is applying only the three claimed edits to the new dump and taking the hash again. Re-run and it reproduces: `jq -S -c . test/tmp/datastage/base-settings.json | shasum -a 256` is f83e037d8f787dcfbbaaae604a851154abb80800b9b43c21d96c5007c583d70e, and the same dump with element [9] deleted from `bbb-recipe-cost`, element [4] deleted from each of the two text settings, and the old closing sentence ("
A text this mod cannot use is set aside and that default applies instead; the reason is in the log, or in the load error if the load stops anyway.") put back on both, is b6e583e6163249ba163dd5051bd835970818cb0a9bba1785359c29f0e46cd26f, which is the row this one replaced, to the byte. ONE, `bbb-recipe-cost`'s composed `localised_description` gains a line between its wrap line and its switch line saying that where an option names something your mods do not have the next name it offers is used instead, that an entry it offers nothing for is left out, that two landing on one name have their amounts added, and that what you craft can therefore be a shorter list than the one shown. TWO, both text settings gain the same disclosure in their own words, the ingredient one about names and the pack one about science packs, in the slot between their wrap line and their format line. THREE, both text settings' closing fallback line says the field behaves as though it said default where it said that default applies instead, which is this repository's own migration finding 19 answered: the target of a fallback is the dropdown's CURRENT preset and not this mod's declared list, so naming a default was false on five presets of six. `bbb-tech-cost` is unmoved, because a cost dropdown carries neither a wrap line nor a ladder line; so are both research numbers. Both `prototype_list_checksum` values are unmoved and both `data_raw_sha256` values are unmoved, and since the DATA-RAW hash is taken over the whole normalised dump its being unmoved IS those dumps compared byte for byte, which is what says the library round reaches the settings stage and nothing else while every setting is at its default. THAT IT DID NOT MOVE IS ITSELF THE CHECK the library asked for: fix round 3 also changed what a prototype carrying a note emits, and a data hash moving here would have been an ingredient list resolving differently on the declared defaults, which is worth finding before it ships.
